## Overview

**Voragos, The Ashen Winged Eclipse** — an Ancient Black Dragon of such immense age that few living creatures could remember a time before he darkened the skies. Among the Five Great Generals, Voragos served as the Scourge's living instrument of annihilation, deployed only when conquest ceased to matter. He was the first of the Great Generals to fall, slain by the greatest heroes of the First Alliance in one of the bloodiest confrontations of the entire Scourge War.

---

## Species

Ancient Black Dragon. Even among dragonkind, he was regarded as an ancient relic from a forgotten age. He was not merely an Ancient Dragon — he was one of the oldest living creatures ever to march beneath the banner of the Scourge.

---

## Title

**The Ashen Winged Eclipse.** Over the centuries, kingdoms gave him many names. Some called him The Black Death of the Skies and others The End of Kingdoms. Yet history remembers only one: The Ashen Winged Eclipse. For wherever Voragos flew, only ash and darkness remained.

---

## Appearance

Voragos was an immense Ancient Black Dragon whose size eclipsed nearly every other creature upon the battlefield. His scales resembled polished obsidian, absorbing light rather than reflecting it, while countless scars carved across his body bore witness to centuries of warfare. Great horns swept backwards from his skull like jagged crowns, broken and reforged by battle after battle. His enormous wings stretched across the battlefield like storm clouds; their weathered membranes stained with soot and ash accumulated through centuries of fire and destruction. His eyes burned with pitch black darkness, never displaying rage or excitement — only cold certainty.

When Voragos took flight, entire battlefields fell into shadow beneath his wings. Long before his fire reached the ground, his silhouette alone was enough to send armies into retreat.

---

## Personality

Voragos embodied the raw instinct of an apex predator. He possessed remarkable intelligence, yet rarely concerned himself with politics, strategy, or conquest beyond what was necessary to fulfill his role within the Scourge. War was not a puzzle to solve; it was a hunt. He viewed every battlefield as his domain, every fortress as prey, and every army as little more than another challenge to overcome through overwhelming force.

Voragos was fiercely proud, even by draconic standards. He tolerated no weakness, respected only power, and considered nearly every living creature beneath his notice. This behavior led to his greatest weakness: his arrogance, which would eventually lead to his unexpected downfall and a turning point in the war.

---

## Philosophy

To Voragos, existence belonged to those capable of claiming it. Civilizations were temporary, and kingdoms were fleeting. Walls, castles, and armies were nothing more than obstacles destined to crumble beneath creatures stronger than those who built them. Voragos believed civilization itself was an illusion. The weak built monuments believing they would last forever; the strong reminded them that nothing ever did. He did not destroy out of hatred, nor cruelty — but because destruction was the purest expression of dominance.

---

## Military Command — The Ashen Legion

Among the Five Great Generals, Voragos served as the Scourge's living instrument of annihilation. He was deployed only when conquest ceased to matter. Entire campaigns changed the moment his Legion entered the battlefield. Rather than prolonged sieges or calculated offensives, Voragos favored relentless aerial assaults designed to shatter every form of organized resistance within hours.

Cities that had withstood months of conventional warfare often fell in a single day beneath his assault. His mere arrival transformed battle plans: defensive formations collapsed, supply lines became meaningless, and fortifications became targets rather than protection. Where Voragos flew, there would be nothing left worth conquering.

Voragos's Ashen Legion was built around speed, devastation, and overwhelming offensive power. Its ranks were dominated by creatures capable of rapid movement and aerial warfare: Dragons, Wyverns, Drakes, Manticores, Chimeras, Flying aberrations, and monstrous predators from every corner of the world. Rather than maintaining rigid formations, Voragos encouraged relentless aggression, allowing each warband to exploit its own strengths while directing the Legion's overall advance through sheer battlefield dominance. The Ashen Legion rarely occupied territory; its purpose was to erase it.

---

## Rise Through the Scourge

Voragos never sought command. Unlike many warlords who climbed through the hierarchy by challenging rivals and expanding their influence through the Gathering of the Spoils, Voragos cared little for rank or authority. He sought only worthy prey.

As his campaigns grew increasingly catastrophic, defeated warbands willingly submitted to his command rather than challenge him, recognizing that survival beneath his wings offered greater glory than certain death opposing them. Over centuries, his following grew into one of the largest Legions the Scourge had ever assembled. His promotion to one of the Five Great Generals was not the result of ambition — it was the inevitable recognition that no other commander could unleash devastation on such an unimaginable scale.

---

## Reputation

Among the mortal races, Voragos became less a creature and more a natural disaster. Entire generations grew up believing that kingdoms did not fall to armies — they fell to Voragos. His appearance alone was enough to trigger mass evacuations long before the first flames reached the horizon. Even the bravest commanders understood that conventional warfare held little meaning once the Ashen Winged Eclipse entered the battlefield. Within the Scourge, Voragos inspired neither loyalty nor admiration — he inspired fear, making respected warlords bow to him.

---

## Fate

During the early years of the First Alliance's Last Stand campaign against the Five Great Generals, Voragos became the Alliance's highest priority. His relentless assaults had reduced entire kingdoms to ash long before conventional armies could even reach the battlefield. So long as the Ashen Winged Eclipse ruled the skies, no fortress could truly be defended, no army could safely march, and no lasting campaign against the Scourge could ever succeed.

Recognizing that the war could not be won while Voragos still lived, the greatest heroes of the Alliance united their strength in a desperate effort to bring him down. The battle that followed became one of the bloodiest confrontations of the entire Scourge War. Though victory came at an unimaginable cost, Voragos was ultimately slain, becoming the first of the Five Great Generals to fall. His death marked the first great victory ever achieved against the Scourge. For the first time since the war had begun, the skies belonged to the mortal races once more.
